evidence.activity: Medicaid managed care health plans for low-income families, children and people with disabilities, the company's largest business
evidence.quote: We are the largest Medicaid health insurer in the country, serving 12.5 million Medicaid members in 30 states as of December 31, 2025.

cross_cultural.criterion: level 4: services built for underserved customers (low-income and disabled Medicaid populations) are a major part of the business, with measured reach

evidence.activity: Voluntary employee-led Centene Professional Networks open to all employees
evidence.quote: Open to all employees, these voluntary, employee-led groups provide professional connections and leadership opportunities for all team members and drive impact by supporting the attraction, development and retention of the best talent at all levels.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Human Capital Resources > Modernized and Connected Workforce

cross_cultural.criterion: level 2: employee networks with no figures

evidence.activity: Centene University internal learning and leadership development platform for employees
evidence.quote: Through Centene University, accessible to our team members, we have designed learning and development at scale, using new digital tools, real-time virtual learnings and customized leadership development programs in a modern learning environment.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Human Capital Resources > Talent Acquisition and Development

community.criterion: level 2: employee development of any size

evidence.activity: Paid volunteer time for employees to support local communities
evidence.quote: In addition, we offer paid community volunteer time to encourage our team members to participate in volunteer programs and support local communities.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Human Capital Resources > Compensation and Other Benefits

community.criterion: level 2: specific current community activity, limited in disclosed reach (no figures)

evidence.activity: Partnership with the National Association of Community Health Centers to strengthen community health centers
evidence.quote: For example, we entered into a partnership with the National Association of Community Health Centers to enhance value-based care adoption, further strengthening Community Health Centers' ability to deliver high-quality, patient-centered care and improve maternal child health outcomes.

community.criterion: level 2: specific current partnership with a nonprofit, no reach figures

evidence.activity: Commercial health insurance sold to small employer groups
evidence.quote: We offer commercial health insurance products to individuals through the ACA Health Insurance Marketplace, and through large and small employer groups in limited areas.

entrepreneurship.criterion: level 1: small-business customers with no specific enabling service

creativity.reason: Level 0: the business description of a managed care insurer is detailed and shows no creative activity.

community.reason: Level 2: it describes employee development (Centene University) plus paid volunteer time and a community health center partnership, but discloses no reach figures, so it does not reach level 3.

cross_cultural.reason: Level 4: health coverage built for underserved low-income and disabled populations is a major part of the business, with measured reach (12.5 million Medicaid members in 30 states); it was not set to 5 because the theme's cultural and language focus is only partly matched, so the lower level was chosen.

entrepreneurship.reason: Level 1: it serves small employer groups as customers but describes no specific service aimed at helping founders or small businesses start or grow.

ai.notes: Cross-cultural scoring: the filing calls Centene 'the nation's largest managed care company focused on underserved populations' and says Medicaid is 57% of external revenues. That 57% figure sits in a separate segment paragraph, so it is not cited as an E1 indicator. Level 5 was considered but not chosen because the populations served are defined mainly by income and disability, with 'culturally sensitive healthcare services' mentioned only generally. A human reviewer may want to reconsider 4 versus 5. E2 professional networks are described as professional and talent groups, not identity or culture groups, so they support level 2 at most. Paid volunteer time and the NACHC partnership disclose no figures. 'Physician and patient educational programs' is mentioned only in passing and is not scored. Past or ending activities, recorded for context only: MMPs ended December 31, 2025; the New Mexico Medicaid contract ended June 2024; the Magellan Health divestiture was signed December 2025. The filing points to a Corporate Responsibility Report but also describes specific activities itself, so coverage is sufficient and no second look is triggered. Traps excluded: 'community engagement' work requirements under the OBBBA, 'Community Medical Group' and 'Community Care' subsidiary names, 'model training' for AI, compliance 'training and education', 'health equity' as general language, 'diversified offerings', and 'identity of our competitors'.
